name: Union Carbide high-performance carbon yarn
description: Union Carbide developed a high-modulus carbon yarn made from rayon-derived fibers, marketed as Thornel 25.

impact.note: One firm's rayon-based high-modulus yarn served a narrow aerospace niche and was soon overtaken by other precursor routes, leaving few direct successors.

date.label: Late 1965
date.basis: The stated range or year applies to the described evidence or documentary event; it does not establish invention.

events.statement: ACS dates the beginning of Union Carbide’s high-modulus yarn series with Thornel 25 to late 1965.

evidence.supports: ACS dates the beginning of Union Carbide’s high-modulus yarn series with Thornel 25 to late 1965.

evidence.locator: Currently Available Structural Carbon Fibers, p. 8
evidence.supports: The NASA memorandum reports a conflicting 1959 introduction date for the commercial Thornel 25 product.

contributions.resource: Development of the Thornel 25 high-modulus yarn

evidence.supports: ACS dates the beginning of Union Carbide’s high-modulus yarn series with Thornel 25 to late 1965.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest sourced event for this particular case, not a claim of global priority.

caveats: ACS dates the start of the yarn series to late 1965 but does not establish the exact date of a commercial sale or continuous manufacture. A 1970 NASA memorandum gives a conflicting 1959 introduction date; the product chronology needs further primary documentation.

research.note: Independent review checked ACS product series, developer, date and reported modulus; commercial timing and manufacturing continuity remain unresolved.

measures.subject: Thornel 25 yarn
measures.conditions: Nominal reported modulus of the 1965 Thornel 25 product; ACS also gives about 172 GPa.

evidence.supports: ACS reports 25 million psi, about 172 GPa, for Thornel 25.
